frozen_at: P-037 A2.2-0 (F0', corrected freeze on main@23e3203)
completeness: Completeness means every candidate occurrence at a call-related syntax site is either represented by the raw guarded-call vocabulary or assigned exactly one named exclusion. Occurrence alone does not establish ownership flow to the enclosing callee.

classes.direct: The argument expression IS a handle identifier (a disposable candidate local or an owned parameter of this method), or the handle is the receiver of a reduced extension method (declared ordinal 0). The value reaches the callee's declared parameter through no conversion or a value-preserving built-in one. Represented: var / param.
classes.transparent: The handle under a transparent wrapper: parentheses, the null-forgiving `!`, or a cast / `as` whose semantic conversion is built-in and value-preserving (identity or a guaranteed reference conversion) and invokes no user-defined operator. The same value reaches the callee. Relevance is kept; the representation is the unwrapped fact (var / param). SyntaxKind alone never makes a cast or an `as` transparent: the conversion does.
classes.may_value: The argument's value is one of several alternatives and a handle is among them, reachable through allowed value-preserving edges only: the conditional operator, null-coalescing `??`, a switch expression, and an `as` whose conversion may fail to null (a downcast the static type does not guarantee). Relevance is kept; the representation stays opaque. An alternative whose value passes through a user-defined conversion is not a handle alternative.
classes.call_like: A genuine call site that is not an invocation expression: object creation (a constructor call), delegate invocation. Each gets its own call fact with the site's own callee; one semantic family per A2.2 commit.
classes.indirect: The handle occurs below the argument, but the value that reaches the callee is something else (a call result, a container, a tuple, a closure, a converted value), or the site binds no summary parameter at all (an ordinary receiver, a storage assignment, a method group). Not relevant to the enclosing callee. Every such occurrence must match exactly one named exclusion below.

conversion_edges.none: identity conversion only; no conversion syntax on the path
conversion_edges.identity: an explicit cast or `as` to the handle's own static type
conversion_edges.reference_upcast: a built-in reference conversion to a base type or an interface, implicit at the parameter or written as a cast / `as`; guaranteed to preserve the value
conversion_edges.may_fail_null: an `as` to a type the handle's static type does not guarantee; yields the handle or null at runtime
conversion_edges.user_defined_implicit: a user-defined implicit operator applied without cast syntax; a hidden call
conversion_edges.user_defined_explicit: a user-defined implicit or explicit operator applied behind cast syntax; a hidden call inside the cast expression
conversion_edges.not_applicable: the handle's value does not reach the parameter at all (indirect occurrence)

conversion_rules: transparent and direct rows carry only none, identity or reference_upcast; never may_fail_null and never a user-defined edge
a user-defined edge, implicit or explicit, is always the named exclusion user_conversion and never transparent, whatever the syntax around it
may_fail_null is always may_value with form as_may_fail, and as_may_fail always carries may_fail_null

A2.2-1 decides these with a value-flow walker over Roslyn IOperation, ClassifyValueFlow(operation, handle) -> Direct | MayValue | Indirect(named_exclusion) | None, checking the semantic conversion at every IConversionOperation on the path and the argument's InConversion; SyntaxKind alone decides nothing, and GetConversion on the whole argument is not enough because (Box)r already has type Box at the call

nested_call_result.definition: The handle is an argument of an INNER invocation whose result is the outer argument. The inner call carries its own call fact (the handle is direct there); the outer call receives call_result, not the handle.

container_construction.definition: The handle is an element of an array, collection or object initializer. The container flows to the callee, not the handle. The initializer's hidden Add call is not a call site of this vocabulary.
container_construction.example: Use3(new Stream[] { r }); new List<Stream> { r }

tuple_construction.definition: The handle is a tuple element. The tuple flows to the callee.

closure_capture.definition: The handle is captured by a lambda, anonymous function or local function that is the argument. The closure flows to the callee; the call inside the lambda belongs to the lambda body (spec/OwnIR.md §5.2), not to this method. Recording the outer call as receiving the handle would be a false raw fact.

method_group_conversion.definition: A method group whose receiver is the handle is converted to a delegate. The delegate flows to the callee.

receiver_not_summary_parameter.definition: The handle is the receiver of an ordinary (non-extension) instance call. The frozen OwnIR binds arguments and reduced-extension receivers only; an ordinary receiver has no declared ordinal, and a summary of `this` is a §10.1 case-5 contract amendment, never a raw fact.

storage_assignment.definition: The handle is assigned into an indexer, a property or a field. An assignment is not a call site of this vocabulary, whatever accessor it compiles to.

user_conversion.definition: The handle reaches the callee through a conversion edge whose Roslyn semantic conversion is user-defined, implicit or explicit, including one hidden inside a cast expression: a hidden call. Unsupported semantic surface in A2, classified but not represented; it may earn its own raw fact later, by amendment. This rule wins over any transparent-looking syntax around it.
user_conversion.example: TakeBox(r) with `implicit operator Box(MemoryStream)`; TakeXBox((XBox)r) with `explicit operator XBox(MemoryStream)`

nameof_operand.definition: The identifier is the operand of nameof. No value flows.

member_access_on_handle.definition: A member of the handle flows, not the handle.

fixture_obligation: Every exclusion has a positive fixture (the rule fires and no call fact is emitted for that site) and a negative fixture (a syntactically adjacent case that is captured instead). A2.2-4 checks both by name; until then the probe below pins the classification.
already_landed_at_a_prime: Relevance and representability are already decoupled for one family at A' (5a0de070): a handle bound to a params slot, passed by ref/out, or an unstable owned parameter is opaque AND keeps the call relevant (corpus/p037-shapes/sidecar-relevance-*). A2.2-1 extends the same separation to the transparent and may-value classes.
known_gaps: Lambda and local-function bodies have no function record of their own, so the calls inside them are unobserved through A2. Recorded as a census finding (§10.1 case 3), not repaired by pretending the enclosing call received the handle.
production_representation_rulings: No `mentions` field in the production sidecar: opaque stays opaque as frozen in spec/OwnIR.md §5.2 and §10.2. A `mentions` list may exist in oracle/debug records only.
No pseudo-ordinal for an ordinary instance receiver (no -1, no `this`, no `receiver: true`).
Closure capture is a named exclusion at the outer call, never a call fact with an opaque handle.
